cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Efficiency Win
cards.instruction: Celebrate each inconvenience as proof that a faster, cheaper, or smarter routine can now be invented.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The dishwasher's broken. Excellent: we'll serve the curry in rolls. No plates to wash.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are twelve guests and only six rolls.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Halve them. Open sandwiches: twice the servings, same bread.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hollow them out first. Edible bowls, and the crumbs thicken the curry. We've saved the flour too.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A3 restricts questions, but A5 practical redesign does not clearly continue the approval relationship.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 six rolls for twelve causes A3 halves; B4 runoff causes A5 hollowing and crumbs, after a preface that answers no question.

relationship.evidence: B2 counts portions and B4 anticipates a physical serving problem, credibly helping make the plan usable.

heightening.evidence: B4 failure of open sandwiches yields A5 edible bowls and thickening reuse, adding a second efficiency.

specificity.evidence: A1 broken dishwasher and curry, B2 guest and roll counts establish concrete constraints.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 saved flour is earned by B4 runny curry and the hollowing byproduct; the stock A3 authority sentence is clumsy.
